test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 08 Sept, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A shopkeeper marks a product 40% above the cost price. He offers a discount of 20% on the marked price and sells it. What is his gain or loss percentage?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net Profit / Loss % can be calculated directly using the successive percentage change formula: a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100

Here, Markup % (a) = +40% and Discount % (b) = −20%

Net % = 40 − 20 + (40 × (−20)) ÷ 100

Net % = 20 − 8 = +12%

Since the result is positive, it indicates a net gain of 12%.

**∴ The correct answer is 12% gain.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 

 

 Markup +40%

 

 Discount −20%

 

 Net Profit +12%

 
 CP: 100

 
 MP: 140

 
 SP: 112

**Given:**

⇒ Markup % = 40%

⇒ Discount % = 20%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Cost Price (CP) be 100 units.

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = CP + (40% of CP) = 100 + 40 = 140

⇒ The shopkeeper allows a 20% discount on the Marked Price.

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = MP − (20% of MP)

⇒ SP = 140 − (20 ÷ 100 × 140)

⇒ SP = 140 − 28 = 112

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 112 − 100 = 12

⇒ Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 = (12 ÷ 100) × 100 = 12%

**∴ The correct answer is 12% gain.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

A discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP), never on the Cost Price (CP). The Selling Price (SP) is obtained after deducting the discount: SP = MP × (100 − D%) ÷ 100.

Successive Discount

When two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the single equivalent discount percentage is given by (a + b − (a × b ÷ 100))%.

Dishonest Dealer Concept

If a trader professes to sell his goods at CP but uses a false weight to deceive the customer, his true Profit % is given by: (Error ÷ False Weight) × 100.
